subject: Re: Clarifying minimum commit + burst pricing for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Minimum commit + burst pricing questions

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We like Redwood's latency profile and the caching features. Two procurement items we need clarified before moving to legal:

1) Minimum monthly commit: what is the smallest commit you can do that still qualifies for the tiered discount?
2) Overage/on-demand rate above commit: how is burst billed — a flat overage per-token or a stepped rate depending on usage?
3) Can bursts be routed to on-demand (no commit) pricing when we exceed committed capacity, and is there a cap on burst unit cost?

We have a rough forecast in the attached spreadsheet. Our finance lead asked for a simple example (commit of 2M tokens/month, usage of 3.2M tokens in a month) showing total monthly spend under your proposal.

Could you send a clear table and suggested contractual language for minimum spend and overage rates?

—Jordan
Senior Product Manager
Acme Retail
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 12:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Minimum commit + burst pricing questions

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Attached is a short proposal (redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf) plus a worked example for the 2M commit scenario. Short answers up front:

- Minimum commit: we can do a 500k tokens/month minimum at the base enterprise tier. Discounts start at 500k but meaningful tiered discounts kick in at 1M and 5M.
- Overage/burst billing: bursts above your committed tokens are billed on-demand per-token at the on-demand rate for the model family. For customers with a commit, we also offer an "overage discount" for predictable bursts: a fixed overage rate between on-demand and commit unit price (see table).
- Routing & cap: bursts are automatically routed to on-demand capacity. We can add a contractual maximum per-token burst cap for the first 3 months (to de-risk your CFO), after which standard overage rules apply.

Attached: redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf (includes tables) and a quick example: 2M commit, 3.2M usage -> commit covers 2M at commit price; 1.2M at overage rate (we show two overage options). I'll flag legal language for minimum spend and overage cap in the doc.

If acceptable, we can produce a one-page amendment that your procurement/legal can sign.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal pages, pricing table)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Minimum commit + burst pricing questions

Ben — forwarding Jordan's note + your draft. A couple of internal points before we finalize with Acme:

- Margin check: Karthik, can you confirm that the 500k minimum + proposed overage discount preserves our target gross margin for the Enterprise tier? If we add a 3-month burst cap, what does that do to tail risk?
- Legal wording: Tessa, Ben included a suggested burst cap for the first 3 months. We need a short, procurement-friendly clause: (a) commit amount, (b) overage rate, (c) burst cap expressed as $/1k tokens not to exceed X, and (d) a waterfall for routing (commit -> dedicated burst pool -> on-demand). Keep it simple so Acme's legal can sign quickly.

Ben, Karthik and Tessa — cc'ing to stay aligned.

—M

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Minimum commit + burst pricing questions

Quick economics note:

- 500k minimum at the base enterprise price (P_base) gives us a 52% gross margin assuming current model mix; acceptable.
- For the 2M commit / 3.2M usage scenario: if we offer an overage discount of 25% off on-demand for the first 1M overage and then full on-demand beyond that, our blended margin stays above 45%.
- The 3-month burst cap expressed as a hard $ cap (e.g., not to exceed $18k/mo in burst charges) removes tail risk and is unlikely to be triggered given Acme's forecast. We should make the cap optional and time-boxed in the amendment.

Tessa, suggested procurement clause below (one-liner):
"Customer commits to a minimum monthly usage of X tokens. Usage beyond the committed amount will be billed at the overage rate specified in the SOW. For the first 90 days post-execution, exceedances up to Y tokens/month will be billed at a capped overage rate of $Z per 1k tokens (the 'Burst Cap'). After 90 days, standard overage terms apply unless otherwise agreed in writing."

I think that's concise and procurement-friendly.

Karthik
Applied ML / Pricing Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Minimum commit + burst pricing questions — revised proposal

Jordan —

Attached is an updated one-page amendment and an example invoice showing the 2M commit / 3.2M usage with two overage options:

Option A (standard):
- Commit: 2,000,000 tokens at $0.0045 per 1k tokens
- Overage: on-demand rate $0.0120 per 1k tokens -> 1,200,000 tokens overage = $14.4k
- Total month = commit charge + overage = $9k + $14.4k = $23.4k

Option B (protected burst):
- Commit: same as above
- Overage: capped overage for first 1M overage at $0.0080 per 1k tokens; remaining overage at on-demand
- For 1.2M overage: 1M at capped rate = $8k; 200k at on-demand = $2.4k -> total overage = $10.4k
- Total month = $9k + $10.4k = $19.4k

Suggested amendment language (single paragraph for procurement):
"Customer commits to a minimum monthly usage of 2,000,000 tokens. Usage beyond the committed amount will be billed at the overage rate set forth in the Pricing Table. For the first 90 days following the Effective Date, Customer's overage charges are subject to a capped overage rate up to 1,000,000 tokens per month as set forth in the Pricing Table; any usage above that capped amount will be billed at the on-demand rate. After 90 days, standard overage terms apply unless otherwise agreed in writing."

If that looks good, I'll generate a DocuSign link and loop Legal for the SOW amendment. We can also reduce the initial commit to 1M if Acme wants a smaller starting commitment — happy to run the numbers.

Cheers,
Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Jordan's reply expected: sign-off or request to drop commit to 1M and adjust cap.
